title: Filtering the sales table by numbers · part 21

steps.title: Keep employee_id < 6
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where employee_id is smaller than 6.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM sales.
Add WHERE after the table name.
The test is employee_id < 6.
Write: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows employee_id < 6
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6;
hints: Start with SELECT count(*).
FROM sales.
Add WHERE employee_id < 6.
Write: SELECT count(*) FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT count(*) FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6;
steps.memory_trick: count(*) + WHERE = 'how many pass?'

steps.title: Filter then sort: employee_id < 6
steps.prompt:
Filter first, then ORDER BY tidies what is left.
LIMIT 3 keeps the top of that sorted list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6 ORDER BY employee_id LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM sales.
Add WHERE employee_id < 6.
Add ORDER BY employee_id LIMIT 3.
Write: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6 ORDER BY employee_id LIMIT 3;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM sales WHERE employee_id < 6 ORDER BY employee_id LIMIT 3;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE trims, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT cuts.
